surface_forms: Monsieur de Guermantes-Bouillon, prince des Laumes

appraisal_events.evidence: « À cause du même besoin maladif de nouveautés arbitraires... » ; « Cette dépravation m'aida à comprendre celle dont faisait preuve Mme de Guermantes » ; « Comme gâtées par la nullité de la vie mondaine, l'intelligence et la sensibilité de Mme de Guermantes étaient trop vacillantes » ; « en faire savourer l'originalité psychologique et briller la malveillance lapidaire ».
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator diagnoses the duchess's celebrated reversals of judgment as a diseased craving for arbitrary novelty, aligning her with the critique folle that saves a horn note from Tristan and discards Molière, and concluding that her mind and sensibility have been spoiled by the emptiness of social life; her paradoxes are shown to prize lapidary malice and effect over truth.

appraisal_events.evidence: « Les variations de jugement de la duchesse n'épargnaient personne, excepté son mari. Lui seul ne l'avait jamais aimée ; en lui elle avait senti toujours un de ces caractères de fer... sous la seule loi desquels les nerveux savent trouver le calme. » ; « souvent de mauvaise humeur contre sa femme, il était fier d'elle » ; « c'était justement le rôle où excellait M. de Guermantes ».
appraisal_events.explanation: The duc is singled out as the one person immune to his wife's devaluations, precisely because he never loved her and is indifferent to her caprices and contemptuous of her beauty, an iron will under which her nervousness finds calm; he also draws standing from her universally acknowledged supremacy and from his own skill at launching the attacks her sentimental reputation forbids her to begin.

status_effects.explanation: The sustained narrator analysis reframes her famous discernment as arbitrary, capricious, and hollowed out by boredom, and her wit as calculated malice rehearsed for an audience.

Her power to revalue people stops at her husband, on whose unloving hardness she depends for calm, and she must rely on him to open the attacks she cannot begin herself; her enthusiasms also decay into irritation she wrongly blames on her admirers.
He holds the only position of leverage in the marriage: exempt from her reappraisals, unmoved by her beauty or her caprices, and the source of the steadiness she needs.

He gains locally by association with a wife whom everyone holds the most beautiful, virtuous, intelligent and cultivated woman of the aristocracy, who covers his disorders and keeps their salon first in the Faubourg Saint-Germain.

ambiguities: The Cambremer verdicts are explicitly counterfactual (« si elle eût vécu alors dans ce milieu, elle eût décrété que Mme de Cambremer était stupide »): they illustrate the duchess's method rather than constituting an actual local appraisal, so no status movement is recorded for either Cambremer despite the strong evaluative wording.

The parliamentary vignette names « M. de Guermantes, prince des Laumes », i.e. the duc under his earlier title; the reference sheet keeps that name-view separate, so the vignette's light irony about performing for the Méséglise electorate is not carried into the duc de Guermantes status effects.
